name: Madhubani (Mithila) Painting

materials.materials_used: Natural pigments derived from flowers (marigold, rose), turmeric, indigo, soot, rice paste on handmade paper or tussar silk.

techniques: Double line drawing filled with intricate cross-hatching, fine line work (Kachni) and solid mineral colour wash (Bharni).
historical_context: Geometric and nature-inspired traditional painting using natural dyes, twigs, nibs, and fingers, originally created on fresh mud-plastered walls.
description: Geometric and nature-inspired traditional painting using natural dyes, originally created on mud-plastered walls.
materials_used: Natural pigments, turmeric, indigo, rice paste, handmade paper, tussar silk, brushes.

name: Jaipur Blue Pottery

materials.materials_used: Ground quartz stone, glass, Katira Gond (gum), Saajji (natural sodium), Fuller's earth, cobalt oxide, and copper oxide.

techniques: Dough is rolled into flat cakes, pressed into plaster molds, hand-painted with cobalt blue and copper oxide, glazed, and kiln-fired once.
historical_context: Turquoise-glazed quartz pottery with Persian and Central Asian motifs, uniquely made without clay using ground quartz stone, glass, and natural gums.
description: Turquoise-glazed pottery with Persian and Central Asian motifs, made without clay using ground quartz stone.
materials_used: Ground quartz stone, glass, natural gums, Fuller's earth, cobalt oxide, copper oxide.

name: Banarasi Kadhwa Brocade Weaving

materials.materials_used: Mulberry silk yarn, pure silver electroplated gold zari thread, hand-punched Jacquard and pit loom warp.

techniques: Traditional Kadhwa technique where each floral motif is individually engraved by hand without loose float threads behind the fabric.
historical_context: Opulent handloom silk brocades woven with genuine gold and silver zari threads, featuring Mughal floral jaal, paisley (kalka), and bel motifs.
description: Opulent silk brocades woven with gold and silver zari threads, featuring Mughal floral jaal, paisley (kalka) and bel motifs.
materials_used: Mulberry silk yarn, pure silver/gold zari thread, Jacquard loom, pit loom.

name: Agra Marble Inlay (Pietra Dura)

materials.materials_used: Makrana white marble, semi-precious stones (lapis lazuli, malachite, cornelian, jasper, turquoise, mother of pearl), natural adhesives.

techniques: Stones are sliced, ground on diamond emery wheels, fitted into carved marble depressions with sub-millimeter tolerances, and polished with zinc oxide.
historical_context: Intricate lapidary technique of cutting and inlaying semi-precious gemstones into white Makrana marble, identical to the Taj Mahal ornamentation.
description: Exquisite marble inlay using semi-precious stones to create intricate floral and geometric designs.
materials_used: Marble, semi-precious stones (carnelian, lapis lazuli, malachite, jade, onyx), natural adhesives.

name: Warli Tribal Painting

materials.materials_used: Rice flour paste, water, gum binder applied on mud-and-cow-dung plastered walls or natural canvas with chewed bamboo twigs.

techniques: Monochromatic white pigment hand-painted onto reddish-ochre background in continuous rhythmic scenes without shading.
historical_context: Minimalist indigenous tribal painting using basic geometric shapes—circles, triangles, and lines—to depict everyday village life, harvest dances, and Mother Earth.
description: Minimalist yet expressive art using simple geometric shapes depicting village life, nature and traditions.
materials_used: Natural clay, rice paste, bamboo sticks, earthy pigments.

name: Kumartuli Terracotta Art

materials.materials_used: Ganga silt clay (entel mati), bamboo armature, rice straw (khor), jute twine, tamarind seed paste, water-based natural pigments.

techniques: Bamboo frames are bound with straw, coated with multiple layers of silt clay, dried naturally, detailed with facial molds, painted and dressed in sholapith.
historical_context: Centuries-old sculpting tradition where artisan families fashion monumental divine idols using Hooghly River alluvial silt and biodegradable materials.
description: Traditional clay sculptures and idols handcrafted for festivals and decorative art, with a unique regional style.
materials_used: Natural clay, river silt, natural dyes, traditional tools.

name: Raghurajpur Pattachitra Cloth & Palm Leaf Painting

materials.materials_used: Treated cotton cloth with tamarind seed paste and chalk powder, dried palm leaves (Tala Pattachitra), natural sea-shell white, lamp black, hingula red.

techniques: Etching on dried palm leaves with iron stylus followed by lamp-black rubbing, and delicate fine brush drawing on prepared cloth canvas.
historical_context: Cloth-based scroll painting known for intricate mythological narratives, fine brush strokes, floral borders, and natural mineral colours.

name: Assam Muga Golden Silk Weaving

materials.materials_used: Muga golden silk filament, traditional bamboo throw-shuttle looms (Taat Xaal).

techniques: Hand-reeled wild silk filaments hand-woven with traditional Assamese geometric motifs like Kingkhap and Japi on handlooms.
historical_context: Rare, shimmering natural golden-yellow wild silk produced exclusively by the endemic Antheraea assamensis silkworm in Assam.

name: Kanchipuram Silk Sarees (Kanjeevaram)

materials.materials_used: Mulberry silk threads, silver zari electroplated with pure 24k gold

techniques: Hand-loom weaving with Korvai interlocking border technique and Petni body-pallu attachment.
historical_context: Heavy mulberry silk sarees woven with pure gold and silver dipped zari, distinguished by contrasting borders joined using the ancient Korvai interlocking technique.

name: Jaipur Blue Pottery

materials.materials_used: Quartz stone powder, katira gum, sajji, copper and cobalt oxide pigments

techniques: Non-clay mould formulation, hand-painting with squirrel hair brushes, single firing in low-fire wood kilns.
historical_context: Unique non-clay ceramic craft made from powdered quartz stone, Fuller's earth, glass, and gum, fired only once and adorned with cobalt oxide blue floral motifs.
description: Turquoise-glazed pottery with Persian and Central Asian motifs, made without clay using ground quartz stone.
materials_used: Ground quartz stone, glass, natural gums, Fuller's earth, cobalt oxide, copper oxide.

name: Channapatna Wooden Toys & Lacquerware

materials.materials_used: Wrightia tinctoria ivory wood, button lac, turmeric, indigo, kumkum vegetable pigments

techniques: Wood turning on manual and power lathes, dry rubbing with pigmented natural shellac sticks, leaf polishing.
historical_context: Eco-friendly wooden toys hand-turned on lathes using soft Wrightia tinctoria (Aale Mara) ivory wood and polished with non-toxic natural vegetable dyes and shellac.

name: Aranmula Kannadi (Front-Surface Metal Mirror)

materials.materials_used: Secret bell-metal bronze alloy (copper, tin, and herbal extracts), clay crucibles

techniques: Lost-wax casting of bronze alloy disc followed by weeks of manual polishing with velvet cloth and herbal paste.
historical_context: Mystical handheld metal alloy mirrors with zero secondary refraction; front-surface reflection created through a closely guarded copper-tin metallurgical proportion.

name: Kashmir Pashmina & Kani Shawl

materials.materials_used: Changthangi Capra hircus down wool (12-15 microns), walnut wood looms

techniques: Hand-spinning on Yinder charkha, weaving with needle-like wooden eyeless bobbins following Talim coded design scripts.
historical_context: Ultra-fine hand-spun underfleece of Himalayan Changthangi goats woven on wooden looms using miniature wooden spools (Kanjis) following coded Talim musical notation graphs.
description: Ultra-fine hand-spun pashmina woven with intricate Kani technique, featuring traditional motifs inspired by nature, Persian art and Kashmiri heritage.
materials_used: Pashmina wool (Changthangi goat), natural dyes, wooden looms, Kani weaving sticks (tujis).

name: Dokra Bell Metal Lost-Wax Casting

materials.materials_used: Brass scrap, pure beeswax, riverbed clay, charcoal and cow dung kilns

techniques: Clay core modeling, beeswax thread wrapping, clay outer mould baking, molten brass pouring into cavity.
historical_context: Non-ferrous metal casting using the ancient Cire Perdue (lost-wax) technique, identical to the 4,500-year-old Harappan Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-Daro.
description: Non-ferrous metal casting using the ancient cire perdue (lost-wax) technique, known for its unique tribal motifs and rustic golden finish.
materials_used: Brass scrap, beeswax, riverbed clay, charcoal, natural pigments.

name: Muga Silk of Assam (Golden Silk)

materials.materials_used: Antheraea assamensis endemic golden silk cocoons, traditional fly-shuttle throw looms

techniques: Reeling on Bhir spinning reels, yarn conditioning in alkali baths, handloom weaving of Mekhela Chador.
historical_context: Natural shimmering golden wild silk harvested exclusively from the endemic Antheraea assamensis silkworm; gains luster with each wash and outlives generations.
description: Natural shimmering golden muga silk woven exclusively in Assam, known for its durability, rich texture and natural golden hue that deepens with time.
materials_used: Muga silk yarn, natural dyes, traditional handlooms, bamboo accessories.

name: Thanjavur (Tanjore) Gold Leaf Painting

materials.materials_used: Teakwood plank, limestone gesso paste, 22-karat gold foil leaf, glass cabochons

techniques: Preparation of cloth-over-wood canvas, relief embossing with chalk and gum paste, 22k gold leaf application, natural color filling.
historical_context: Panel painting executed on solid teakwood boards featuring raised gesso relief work encrusted with semi-precious Jaipur stones and pure 22-karat gold foil leaves.
description: Traditional panel painting on wood with raised gesso work, gold leaf and vibrant natural colours, depicting Hindu deities and mythological themes.
materials_used: Teak wood panel, gesso (chalk & glue), gold leaf, natural pigments, semi-precious stones.

name: Muga Silk of Assam

materials.materials_used: Natural golden silk yarn derived from Som and Soalu tree-fed silkworms; woven on traditional throw-shuttle looms.

techniques: Multi-stage manual reeling, degumming, and handloom weaving with Jacquard or traditional drawboy cards.
historical_context: The rarest wild golden silk in the world, produced exclusively in the Brahmaputra Valley by the endemic silkworm Antheraea assamensis. It is naturally golden-yellow, highly durable, and gains luster with every wash.
description: The rare and valuable golden silk of Assam, handwoven with traditional motifs, known for its natural brightness and long lasting strength.
materials_used: Muga silk yarn, natural dyes, traditional handlooms.

name: Majuli Mask Making (Mukha Shilpa)

materials.materials_used: Local bamboo split frames, cane, khagori reeds, pottery clay mixed with cow dung, and natural mineral dyes.

techniques: Bamboo armature construction, papier-mâché layering with clay, hand sculpting, and painting with natural mineral colors.
historical_context: A 500-year-old traditional mask-making tradition practiced at Natun Samaguri Satra on Majuli island, created for Bhaona mythological theatrical performances.
description: Traditional mask-making craft of Majuli, used in Bhaona (theatre) performances, made from natural materials and hand-painted with vibrant colours.
materials_used: Bamboo, cane, clay, cow dung, natural dyes, traditional adhesives.

name: Wancho Beaded Craft & Wood Carving

materials.materials_used: Traditional seed beads, colorful glass beads, local softwoods, and bamboo cane.

techniques: Geometric thread stringing, loom bead-weaving, and handheld chisel carving.
historical_context: Vibrant ceremonial bead jewelry, headdresses, and wooden warrior figures handcrafted by the Wancho tribe of eastern Arunachal Pradesh.
description: Vibrant ceremonial bead jewelry, headdresses, and wooden works of pines handcrafted by the Wancho tribe of eastern Arunachal Pradesh.
materials_used: Natural seeds (beads), colorful glass beads, local timber, bamboo, cane.

name: Monpa Wood Carving & Dapa Vessels

materials.materials_used: Local seasoning maple burl (Ting-shing), pine wood, and vegetable lacquers.

techniques: Loom turning and manual relief chiseling featuring dragons, lotus blossoms, and Tibetan floral scrolls.
historical_context: Exquisite handheld wooden bowls (Dapa), prayer tables (Choktse), and decorative Buddhist masks hand-carved from maple, walnut, and pine woods.
description: Exquisite hand-carved wooden bowls (Dapa), prayer vessels and ritual objects adorned with Buddhist motifs, hand-carved from maple, walnut, and pine woods.
materials_used: Local woods (maple, pine), traditional carving tools, natural and vegetable lacquers.

name: Ryndia (Eri Peace Silk) Weaving

materials.materials_used: Castor-leaf-fed Eri silk yarn, natural botanical dyes derived from lac, turmeric, wild madder, and iron water.

techniques: Drop-spindle hand spinning, botanical dye extraction, and weaving on traditional Khasi ground throw-shuttle looms.
historical_context: An eco-friendly 'Ahimsa' organic silk handwoven from the cocoons of the Philosamia ricini moth without killing the pupae. Celebrated for thermal properties.
artisan_name: Ri Bhoi Eri Silk Weavers Cooperative
description: An eco-friendly Ahimsa (peace) silk handwoven from the cocoons of the Philosamia ricini moth without killing the pupae. Celebrated for its natural texture.
materials_used: Eri silk yarn (spun), natural dyes (plant based), bamboo loom, lac, tamarind, wild madder, and iron-rich mud.

name: Larnai Black Clay Pottery

materials.materials_used: Local Sung clay mixed with serpentinite rock dust, dyed with wild Soh-kew plant extract.

techniques: Hand-moulding using flat wooden mallets and open-fire pit firing with dried leaves and husks.
historical_context: An ancient prehistoric unglazed black pottery tradition practiced exclusively by Pnar women of Larnai village without the use of a potter's wheel.
description: Traditional black clay pottery shaped by hand without potter's wheel using black serpentine clay and wild soh-kew plant extract for natural black finish.
materials_used: Sung clay, serpentine stone powder, wild soh-kew tree bark dye.

name: Naga Handwoven Shawls

materials.materials_used: Indigenous cotton, stinging nettle fiber, and natural vegetable dyes.

techniques: Traditional backstrap loin loom weaving with extra-weft continuous patterning.
historical_context: Distinctive tribal ceremonial shawls featuring bold geometric patterns, clan identities, and animal motifs handwoven on traditional loin looms.
description: Distinctive tribal ceremonial shawls featuring bold geometric patterns, clan identities, and animal motifs handwoven on traditional loin looms.
materials_used: Indigenous cotton, stinging nettle fiber, and natural vegetable dyes.

name: Chakhesang Naga Shawl

materials.materials_used: Wild nettle fiber, locally grown cotton, and natural mineral dyes.

techniques: Laborious manual fiber retting, hand-spinning, and loin loom weaving.
historical_context: Ceremonial shawl woven with hand-spun local nettle fiber and natural colored yarn, featuring the sacred motifs of the Chakhesang tribe.
description: Ceremonial shawl woven with hand-spun local nettle fiber and natural colored yarn, featuring the sacred motifs of the Chakhesang tribe.
materials_used: Wild nettle fiber, locally grown cotton, and natural mineral dyes.

name: Shaphee Lanphee Textile

materials.materials_used: Handspun black cotton fabric, vibrant red, yellow, and green silk embroidery yarn.

techniques: Loin-loom woven fabric base with freehand needlework embroidery without stencils.
historical_context: A magnificent traditional black ceremonial shawl embroidered with red and yellow cosmic motifs (sun, moon, stars) and auspicious animals.

name: Longpi Black Stone Pottery (Hamlei)

materials.materials_used: Ground serpentinite stone and weathering clay mixed in a 5:3 ratio; polished with Chiron na leaves.

techniques: Hand-moulding using flat stone mallets, open-bonfire firing, and polishing with wild leaves to achieve metallic black sheen.
historical_context: An ancient Tangkhul Naga pottery tradition made without a potter's wheel using black serpentinite stone and weathered brown clay.

name: Mizo Puan (Puanchei & Ngotekherh)

materials.materials_used: Pure cotton and acrylic yarn woven on backstrap loin looms.

techniques: Complex supplementary weft patterning requiring extreme mathematical precision and finger manipulation.
historical_context: The national textile wrap of Mizoram, featuring intricate geometric stripes in red, black, and white handwoven on traditional loin looms.

name: Sikkimese Buddhist Thangka Painting

materials.materials_used: Gessoed cotton canvas, natural mineral pigments (malachite, cinnabar, lapis lazuli), 24-carat liquid gold dust, and silk brocade.

techniques: Strict adherence to the iconometric measurements laid down in the Buddhist Kanjur scriptures.
historical_context: Sacred Buddhist scroll paintings of deities, mandalas, and Arhats executed on cotton canvas framed in exquisite silk brocades.

name: Sikkimese Choktse (Carved Folding Table)

materials.materials_used: Tooni and pine seasoned timber, gold paint, and natural lacquers.

techniques: Precision interlocking joint construction without metallic nails; relief carving using fine chisels.
historical_context: Intricately carved folding wooden tea and prayer tables decorated with Buddhist eight auspicious symbols (Ashtamangala) and vivid paints.

name: Tripura Risa Handwoven Textile

materials.materials_used: Locally spun cotton and bright natural dyes.

techniques: Loin loom weaving with traditional warp and weft counts passing down ancestral tribal patterns.
historical_context: A traditional handwoven breastcloth featuring striking geometric motifs and colorful stripes, woven on indigenous loin looms by tribal women.

name: Tripura Bamboo & Cane Screen Craft

materials.materials_used: Muli and Barak native bamboo species seasoned with herbal treatments.

techniques: Hair-thin sliver splitting, delicate warp-weft plaiting, and heat bending.
historical_context: Ultra-fine bamboo split mats, delicate window screens, and lacquered containers showcasing the highest standards of bamboo craftsmanship in India.

name: Ladakh Pashmina (Cashmere)

materials.materials_used: Raw Pashm fiber with a fineness of 12–15 microns.

techniques: Gentle manual combing, traditional wooden spinning wheel ('Yender') processing, and handloom shawl weaving.
historical_context: The world's finest cashmere wool harvested from the Changthangi (Pashmina) goat grazing at 14,000+ feet in the Changthang region. Spun and woven by hand.

name: Ladakh Wood Carving (Shingskos)

materials.materials_used: Poplar, willow, and seasoned Himalayan cedar.

techniques: Deep relief manual gouging and mineral pigment painting.
historical_context: High-relief wood carving on monastery pillars, capital brackets, and carved prayer tables featuring Buddhist dragons, snow lions, and lotus motifs.

name: Lakshadweep Island Coir & Coconut Fiber Craft

materials.materials_used: Lagoon-retted coconut husk fiber and natural sea-salt mineral seasoning.

techniques: Traditional manual husk beating, spinning on two-ply hand wheels, and net knotting.
historical_context: Traditional coir yarn hand-spun from coconut husks retted naturally in coastal saline lagoons. Known for its golden tint, elasticity, and remarkable resistance to seawater rot.

name: Nicobarese Traditional Pandanus Mat

materials.materials_used: Wild Pandanus palm leaves dried and smoothed using sea shells, natural plant stains.

techniques: Manual longitudinal leaf splitting and tight diagonal plaiting without a loom.
historical_context: Delicate, durable sleeping and ceremonial mats handwoven by indigenous Nicobarese women from dried split leaves of the wild Pandanus (screw pine) palm.

name: Villianur Terracotta Craft

materials.materials_used: Green fine silt clay from Villianur tank, river sand, and firewood for kiln reduction.

techniques: Hand sculpting and wheel thrown sections joined using slip clay, open kiln firing without synthetic glazes.
historical_context: Renowned fine terracotta art made from specialized alluvial clay found in the local Villianur tank, celebrated for monumental Ayyanar temple horses and delicate domestic statues.

name: Tirukanur Papier Mâché Craft

materials.materials_used: Recycled cotton paper pulp, plaster of Paris, natural gum, and tempera paints.

techniques: Die pressing, hand finishing, sandpaper smoothing, and traditional polychrome painting.
historical_context: Finely detailed lightweight figurines of classical deities, historical figures, and life-size festival statues made from paper pulp and chalk powder.

name: Warli Bamboo & Palm Craft of Silvassa
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

materials.materials_used: Local bamboo species, wild date palm leaves, and natural plant sap.

techniques: Manual splinter splitting and tight diagonal plaiting.
historical_context: Traditional storage bins, hunting traps, fishing nets, and palm-leaf wall hangings handcrafted by the indigenous Warli and Kokna tribes.

name: Bastar Wrought Iron Craft (Loha Shilp)

materials.materials_used: Scrap iron, charcoal fire, hand hammers, and tongs

techniques: Repeated hot-forging, beating, and twisting over open charcoal hearths
historical_context: An ancient indigenous metalcraft practiced by the blacksmith Luhura community of Bastar, transforming scrap iron into expressive wildlife figurines without molds.

name: Sohrai and Khovar Mural Painting

materials.materials_used: Dhudhi matti (white clay), geru (red ochre), charak matti (black manganese earth), broken combs, and chewed datun twigs

techniques: Layering dark earth undercoat followed by white clay, then incising lines with comb teeth while wet (sgraffito)
historical_context: A traditional ritualistic mural art practiced by indigenous women using natural river clays and combs to etch fertility and wildlife motifs on mud home walls.

name: Sikki Grass Craft of Bihar

materials.materials_used: Wild Sikki grass stems, Munj grass core, natural dye powders, Takua brass needle

techniques: Coiling and stitching wet grass fibers over a structural Munj core using a specialized needle
historical_context: An eco-friendly craft where wild golden Sikki grass (Chrysopogon zizanioides) is dyed into vibrant colours and coomed into durable decorative containers, boxes, and toys.

name: Baluchari Figural Silk Saree

materials.materials_used: Pure mulberry silk yarn, natural vegetable dye extracts

techniques: Intricate jacquard harness weaving requiring two master weavers operating a single loom for up to 20 days per saree
historical_context: An extraordinary handloom silk saree renowned for its ornate pallu depicting narrative mythological scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Nawabi courts.

name: Chanderi Handloom Fabric & Sarees

materials.materials_used: Mulberry silk yarn, high-count unbleached cotton, metallic Zari thread

techniques: Hand-interlocking weft technique (Nal) with delicate bootis inserted by hand
historical_context: A historic lightweight, sheer textile celebrated for its gossamer transparency, delicate silk warp, and shimmering pure gold and silver Zari borders.

name: Gond Tribal Canvas & Paper Painting

materials.materials_used: Acrylic pigments, archival canvas, fine sable brushes, handmade paper

techniques: Freehand outlining followed by signature repetitive geometric pattern infill unique to each family clan lineage
historical_context: A captivating indigenous art tradition characterized by intricate patterns of dots, dashes, and fine lines forming trees of life, forest spirits, and birds.

name: Bidriware Metal Inlay Craft

materials.materials_used: Zinc and copper alloy, pure silver foil/wire, ammonium chloride, and Bidar fort soil

techniques: Sand casting, fine engraving with chisels, silver hammer-inlay, and thermal mud-paste blackening
historical_context: A striking metal handicraft where pure silver wire is inlaid into an alloy of zinc and copper, followed by a unique chemical blackening using local fort soil.
image_attribution: Art Projects MKCL KF / Wikimedia Commons

name: Aranmula Kannadi (Front-Surface Metal Mirror)

materials.materials_used: Secret copper-tin speculum metal alloy, clay molds, velvet polish cloth, brass frames

techniques: Precision lost-wax casting followed by weeks of manual polishing with jute cloth and Marottikkai oil
historical_context: A world-unique handmade metal alloy mirror that eliminates secondary reflections because light reflects directly from the polished front surface rather than glass.

name: Srikalahasti Freehand Kalamkari

materials.materials_used: Unbleached cotton cloth, buffalo milk, bamboo pens, myrobalan nut, alum, natural mineral dyes

techniques: 17-step organic process including milk treatment, freehand charcoal sketching, kalam dye application, and river washing in the Swarnamukhi
historical_context: An ancient temple textile art executed entirely freehand using a bamboo pen (kalam) and vegetable dyes to illustrate epic mythological narratives.

name: Kondapalli Wooden Lacquer Toys (Bommala Koluvu)

materials.materials_used: Tella Poniki softwood, Makku paste (tamarind seed powder and sawdust), natural and enamel paints

techniques: Hand chiseling of light timber, assembly with tamarind glue, and fine oil painting with palm hair brushes
historical_context: Lightweight, charming softwood toys and statuettes representing mythological figures, rural village scenes, and the famous bobblehead dancing doll (Thanjavur-style).

name: Pochampally Tie and Dye Silk-Cotton Ikat

materials.materials_used: Fine mulberry silk, pure cotton yarn, natural and azo-free reactive dyes

techniques: Complex Pagdu Bandhu warp-and-weft tie-dyeing guided by graph blueprints followed by precision loom alignment
historical_context: A legendary textile art where warp and weft yarns are tied and dyed in mathematically precise geometric patterns prior to weaving on pit looms.

name: Rogan Painting of Nirona, Kutch

materials.materials_used: Castor seed oil, natural earth and mineral pigments, brass or iron stylus (kalam)

techniques: Boiling castor oil for 48 hours to create a sticky gel base, rolling fine threads of paste in the palm, applying freehand, and folding the cloth to mirror the pattern
historical_context: A rare 300-year-old art form where boiled castor oil is transformed into a colored paste and applied to fabric using a six-inch metal stylus without directly touching the cloth.

name: Patan Double Ikat Patola Silk

materials.materials_used: Pure mulberry silk, natural dyes (madder root, turmeric, marigold, indigo), catechu

techniques: Hand-tying microscopic threads guided by graph blueprints; handloom operation by two weavers producing 20 centimeters per day
historical_context: The ultimate pinnacle of Indian weaving where both warp and weft silk yarns are resist-dyed before weaving with mathematical precision so that front and reverse sides are identical.

name: Paithani Handloom Silk Saree

materials.materials_used: Pure mulberry silk yarn, fine gold and silver electroplated Zari thread

techniques: Ancient tapestry weaving technique where weft threads are interlocked by hand without shuttle relays
historical_context: Considered the 'Queen of Sarees' in Maharashtra, renowned for its oblique square border design and magnificent pallu featuring the Mor (peacock) and Bangadi Mor motifs.

name: Phulkari Geometric Silk Embroidery

materials.materials_used: Raw khaddar cotton fabric, untwisted Pat floss silk threads, natural dyes

techniques: Darning stitch executed purely by counting threads on the reverse side of fabric without stencils
historical_context: Vibrant folk embroidery where untwisted floss silk thread (Pat) is embroidered from the reverse side of coarse handspun cotton cloth (Khaddar) in intricate geometric patterns.

name: Panipat Punja Handloom Durrie

materials.materials_used: Coarse cotton yarn, wool, natural and fast vat dyes

techniques: Weft-faced flat tapestry weaving where weft yarns are beaten down tightly over warps with the iron Punja
historical_context: Heavy-duty, beautifully patterned reversible flatweave carpets woven on upright looms using the heavy metallic comb-like claw tool called 'Punja'.

name: Kullu Handloom Woolen Shawl

materials.materials_used: Local desi wool, Merino wool, Angora rabbit hair, Pashmina blend

techniques: Dobby loom weaving with intricate geometric patterns inserted by hand using individual colored bobbins
historical_context: Warm, exquisitely crafted handloom woolen shawls characterized by their brilliant geometric borders woven in up to eight bright contrasting colors.

name: Chamba Rumal (Double-Sided Needle Painting)

materials.materials_used: Handspun malmal or khaddar cloth, untwisted Pat silk threads, natural vegetable dyes

techniques: Fine miniature-painting line drawings outlined by master Pahari painters, then filled with dense double-darning embroidery
historical_context: A pictorial needlework tradition executed on unbleached muslin with untwisted silk thread using the 'Do-rukha' stitch, rendering the pattern completely identical on both sides.

name: Uttarakhand Aipan Ritual Folk Art

materials.materials_used: Geru (brick-red wet earth paste), Biswar (soaked ground rice paste), bamboo stylus, fingertips

techniques: Applying the smooth red Geru background on stone or wood, then freehand drawing sacred geometric mandalas (Yantras) with three fingers
historical_context: A ritual folk art practiced by Kumaoni women on floors, thresholds, and prayer seats using red ochre clay and white ground rice flour paste.

name: Kashmir Walnut Wood Carving

materials.materials_used: Locally harvested seasoned walnut root and trunk wood, steel chisels (woor), agate polishing stones

techniques: Under-cutting, relief carving, and deep jaali lattice fretwork followed by natural beeswax or agate-stone rubbing without synthetic polish
historical_context: An exquisite woodcraft using seasoned walnut wood (Juglans regia) native to Kashmir, carved entirely by hand into delicate floral, dragon, and lattice jaali patterns.

name: Kaavi Architectural Sgraffito Murals

materials.materials_used: Urak (fermented palm spirit), sea-shell lime (chunam), red laterite earth (kaav), river sand, steel etching stylus

techniques: Applying wet red laterite plaster, coating with white lime, and incising intricate mythological scenes with a stylus before the mortar sets
historical_context: A rare indigenous Goan mural art found on old Konkani temple and ancestral mansion walls, etched into dark red laterite clay plaster covered with lime wash.

name: Delhi Zardozi Gold & Metallic Embroidery

materials.materials_used: Gilded copper and silver wires, Salma, Dabka, sequins, pearls, silk velvet fabric

techniques: Fabric stretched tightly over wooden frames (Khaat); artisans use wooden-handled hook needles (Ari) to sew metallic coils with two hands
historical_context: An opulent three-dimensional embroidery using fine gold and silver wire (Zari) sewn onto heavy silks and velvets, historically adorning Mughal royal robes and canopies.
